title: Prospective Study on the epileptogenicity of white matter lesions
summary:
In this study we aim to evaluate if alterations of the white matter of the brain are associated with the risk of developing epileptic seizures. Currently, it is believed that only grey matter lesions (where the cell bodies of neurons are located) are responsible for the development of seizures. However, we assume that also lesions of the white matter, which for example develop in patients with elevated blood pressure, are associated with an increased risk of seizures.
 To further evaluate this hypothesis, we aim to include patients who had a first seizure and no alterations of the grey matter. We analyze the MRI images of these patients and check for white matter lesions. If these white matter lesions are present we analyze their size and localization.
12 months after the first seizure, patients will be interviewed on the occurrence of a second seizure. We will then compare the rate of seizure recurrence between patients with white matter lesions and those without white matter lesions.

interventions.name: Patients with first unprovoked seizure and cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD)
Patients with first unprovoked seizure and no cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with first seizure
- Patients with MRI of the head
- age > 59 years
Exclusion criteria:
- epileptogenic lesion in the MRI
- patients unable to provide informed consent
